tasks.short: Resolve escalated customer complaints, agree remedies, and coordinate their completion.

steps.what: Read the complaint and identify its issue, urgency, and owner

loop.input: Complaint text and attachments, with a fixed issue taxonomy and escalation rules.
loop.output: Source-linked facts, requested remedy, proposed category, and explicit uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Require source spans for extracted facts; validate category fields; a manager confirms routing and urgency.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per complaint; unreadable or ambiguous cases return to manual triage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers describe mixed issues in free text; keyword rules alone miss context and negation.

steps.what: Check the account, order history, and previous commitments
Confirm what happened and which recovery options are feasible
Hear the customer's concerns and discuss a workable resolution
Authorise a remedy within delegated limits or escalate approval
Write and send the agreed resolution and next steps

loop.input: Approved remedy, verified facts, customer priorities, and an approved response template.
loop.output: A resolution message containing only authorised commitments.
loop.check: Match amounts, dates, and promises to approved fields; the sales manager checks tone and approves sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one requested revision; unresolved factual conflicts or failed checks require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply the structure, but individual complaints need contextual acknowledgement and plain explanations.

steps.what: Coordinate delivery of the authorised remedy
Confirm acceptance or explain what remains unresolved
Record the outcome and close or reopen the complaint

tasks.design: Join the {HELPDESK} case to account and order history from the {CRM} and {ERP}, using deterministic identity checks and recovery-policy fields. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a case brief and a resolution message, with human gates on routing, remedy authorisation, sending, and closure. The {WORKFLOW} assigns recovery actions and tracks confirmation while people handle the customer conversation and disputed facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts and promises are scattered across service records and correspondence. Free-text complaints resist simple routing rules, while settlement requires clear authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case workflows and record joins handle coordination. Bounded text extraction and drafting can reduce preparation while keeping commitments tied to approved fields.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed evidence, distressed customers, legal claims, and remedies involving several teams remain difficult. Integration cannot make physical recovery work happen.
tasks.human_edge: Restore trust, recognise when a policy-compliant remedy is inadequate, and take responsibility for a credible commitment.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconstructing cases and more time resolving recurring failures with service leads. Remedy limits and formal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Investigate order amendments and delivery discrepancies before proposing recovery
reach.learn: Learn order-event evidence, amendment permissions, and credit escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Record joins, approval limits, ownership, and reminders can be deterministic; negotiated complaint resolution remains human.
HubSpot offers email drafting and outreach components; this is component evidence, not evidence of reliable complaint settlement.
A documented DPD service-chatbot failure supports keeping free-form customer responses constrained and reviewed before sending.
The time allocations and build ranges are estimates; the digest provides no measured outcome for this complaint workflow.

assumptions: This describes escalated complaints needing manager involvement, rather than routine service enquiries.
The task covers coordinating recovery; field repairs, shipment handling, and payment execution belong to their own workflows.
Any financial remedy uses the existing authorised approval route.
GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose limitation, and retention for customer records; EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed use.
No call recording or automatic transcription is assumed.
Build ranges are working-day effort; access and any consultation under national rules can add elapsed time.
unknowns: Complaint volumes, languages, and attachment formats.
Reliable account and order identifiers across systems.
Remedy limits and escalation owners.
Rules for closure, retention, and customer-record access.
research_questions: Which complaint categories can be routed with existing fields and rules alone?
Can brief extraction preserve uncertainty and distinguish allegations from verified facts?
Which response passages actually require contextual drafting beyond approved templates?
new_work: Review extracted facts, routing, and customer messages.
Handle identity mismatches and unresolved evidence.
Maintain remedy limits, templates, and escalation rules.
Sample completed cases for unsupported promises and premature closure.
tasks.statement: Resolve customer complaints regarding sales and service.

tasks.short: Combine customer behaviour and feedback to choose where the sales team should focus.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, repeat-purchase, and win-loss data by customer segment
Retrieve campaign engagement and stated interests by customer segment
Align segments and compare customer signals over time
Read customer comments and identify recurring needs and objections

loop.input: A fixed batch of customer comments and win-loss notes, grouped by approved segment.
loop.output: Cited preference themes, objections, contradictory examples, and unclassified comments.
loop.check: Require record references; calculate counts in code; review samples and retain contradictions and missing coverage.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per batch; ambiguous comments remain unclassified for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers express the same need in different language; fixed keywords do not reliably preserve context.

steps.what: Test apparent preferences against sales representatives' customer experience
Choose segment priorities and a limited sales experiment
Publish approved sales priorities and the experiment brief

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors bring approved fields from the {CRM} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic joins and counts feed a segment dashboard in the {BI}. A bounded classifier groups customer comments with source references, while the manager validates the interpretation and chooses an experiment. A template generator publishes the approved sales focus brief in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Segment definitions and customer identifiers differ across exports. Reading feedback takes time, and engagement measures are easily mistaken for purchase preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and scheduled transformations can maintain a repeatable comparison. Bounded classification can organise text without making the final commercial judgement.
tasks.still_hard: The available customers may be unrepresentative, sales notes may omit lost buyers, and campaign engagement may reflect exposure rather than demand. Commercial experiments still need enough observations and time.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a plausible customer need from a data artefact and choose a commercially useful, testable response.
tasks.altitude: The manager can review segment evidence weekly and spend more time designing and interpreting sales experiments. With an agreed mandate, they can adjust prospecting capacity within existing budget limits.

reach.task: Run discovery interviews to test a segment-specific buying hypothesis
reach.learn: Learn neutral questioning, sampling limits, and how to distinguish stated interest from buying intent.

evidence.claim: Spotler provides lead management, predicted customer value, and campaign-data queries, supporting available customer-signal components.
The Neleman vendor case documents segmentation outcomes; it does not establish results for this sales-focus workflow.
Deterministic aggregation and bounded text classification can prepare evidence, but neither establishes causal customer demand.
Step shares, remaining time, and delivery ranges are estimates rather than customer measurements.

assumptions: The initial scope uses existing customer and campaign records, rather than commissioning a new survey.
Analysis uses approved business segments and excludes inferred sensitive personal attributes.
GDPR applies to personal data and profiling; any resulting outreach must separately meet applicable marketing rules and respect objections.
The proposed weekly cadence is an ambition, not a documented performance result.
Build ranges are working-day effort; access reviews and any consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Customer-identifier coverage between the {CRM} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
Completeness of lost-customer and win-loss feedback.
Permitted analytical uses, retention rules, and suppression handling.
Authority to change prospecting capacity and minimum useful segment sizes.
research_questions: Do behavioural changes persist after accounting for seasonality, exposure, and customer mix?
Does text classification preserve minority needs and contradictory feedback?
Can existing reporting provide the segment comparison without a new data pipeline?
new_work: Maintain segment mappings and data-quality checks.
Review theme samples, contradictions, and unclassified comments.
Design experiments and record outcomes.
Monitor access, retention, and permitted-use rules.
tasks.statement: Monitor customer preferences to determine focus of sales efforts.

tasks.short: Coordinate sales priorities, team actions and customer commitments.

steps.what: Review open opportunities, orders and delivery constraints.
Read team messages and identify blockers requiring coordination.

loop.input: Selected sales issue messages and linked opportunity or order identifiers.
loop.output: Blockers, requested decisions and suggested owners with source references.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and dates; manager checks inferred blockers and ownership.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per brief; ambiguous items remain unassigned.
loop.why_not_simpler: The messages describe blockers in varied free text rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Choose priorities and escalation routes across competing sales opportunities.
Agree responsibilities, deadlines and feasible commitments with sales and operations.
Communicate agreed delivery or commercial commitments to affected customers.

loop.input: Approved commitments and the relevant existing customer correspondence.
loop.output: Customer message draft using only approved commitments.
loop.check: Match dates, prices and scope to approved fields; representative checks tone and recipient.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per message; representative writes unresolved cases.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot cover every negotiated commitment or customer concern.

steps.what: Record owners, next actions and agreed deadlines.
Notify owners and chase overdue agreed actions.
Compare action progress with sales targets and flag deviations.

tasks.design: Configure a shared sales status view from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, with action records and reminders in the {CRM} and {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop extracts blockers from selected {EMAIL} and {CHAT} messages, and another drafts customer messages from approved commitments. Managers agree priorities with people, and representatives approve each external message before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: The activity spans structured records, informal messages and negotiations between teams. Earlier workflows could chase dates but could not reliably interpret varied blocker descriptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task features handle ownership and reminders. Bounded extraction and drafting can now support the informal parts without deciding commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Priorities change, capacity is contested and customer promises can create costly obligations. A dashboard cannot settle those conflicts.
tasks.human_edge: The manager negotiates workable trade-offs and knows when protecting a customer relationship outweighs a short-term sales target.

ambition.what: A weekly joint sales-and-delivery commitment review for complex opportunities.

tasks.altitude: Routine status collection and chasing shrink, leaving more time for cross-team decisions and coaching. The manager can convene earlier commitment reviews; delivery and commercial approval rights remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Confirm technical feasibility before sales commits to scope or delivery.
reach.learn: Acceptance criteria, technical dependencies and how to turn uncertainty into a clear customer commitment.

evidence.claim: A CRM can suggest next actions and provide sales pipeline assistance.
Configured action records and reminders can reduce coordination paperwork.
Bounded extraction and drafting still require checks before customer commitments are communicated.

assumptions: The company coordinates a sales team with an operations or delivery team.
Customer messages concern existing opportunities or orders; marketing outreach needs a separate lawful process.
Only selected business messages are processed, with GDPR access and retention controls.
Time shares give messages and follow-up more weight than the weak mail prior because they connect teams.
Build ranges cover one sales team and existing communication channels.
unknowns: Current ownership of sales actions and delivery approvals.
Whether blockers already have structured fields in the {CRM}.
Permitted access to shared mailboxes and team channels.
Whether employee consultation is required under national rules.
research_questions: Can structured blocker fields eliminate the extraction loop for common cases?
Which reminder thresholds surface useful exceptions without overwhelming owners?
new_work: Review extracted blockers and correct mistaken ownership.
Approve customer drafts and handle sensitive negotiations personally.
Maintain escalation routes and reminder thresholds.
Resolve stale actions and monitor feed failures.
tasks.statement: Direct and coordinate activities involving sales of manufactured products, services, commodities, real estate, or other subjects of sale.

tasks.short: Set price schedules and discount rules.

steps.what: Retrieve product costs, current prices and contractual pricing constraints.
Compare realised prices, discounts, volumes and competitor observations.
Model margin and volume scenarios for proposed price and discount changes.
Choose proposed prices, discount limits and exceptions.
Prepare the price schedule, discount matrix and effective-date notice.
Approve prices, discount authority and the release date.
Update effective prices and discount controls, then notify sales staff.

tasks.design: Use the {ERP} and {CRM} for versioned prices and discount limits, with contractual constraints from the {CLM}. A deterministic calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produces margin scenarios, and configured templates in the {DOCS} generate the schedule and notice. The {WORKFLOW} releases approved versions on their effective date and routes later discounts above delegated limits to the authorised approver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost, contract and realised-price information sat in different records. Existing price controls could enforce a decision but did not provide a joined scenario view.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing price lists and approval features cover publication and enforcement. Small deterministic calculators can now be built and connected with less effort.
tasks.still_hard: Customer response to price changes is uncertain. Contract exceptions, currency treatment and commercial positioning can dominate the arithmetic.
tasks.human_edge: The manager judges willingness to pay, relationship consequences and which exceptions deserve a commercial rationale.

ambition.what: Monthly review of margin leakage from discretionary discounts.

tasks.altitude: Pricing reviews centre on commercial trade-offs rather than rebuilding schedules and calculations. The manager can recommend targeted discount changes more often; release and exception authority follows the approved delegation.

reach.task: Negotiate customer discounts within authorised limits.
reach.learn: Net-price waterfalls, contract exceptions and how to explain value before offering a discount.

evidence.claim: Price schedules, discount matrices and approval thresholds can use deterministic records and workflows.
Scenario calculations can show assumed margin and volume effects without predicting customer response.

assumptions: The {ERP} or {CRM} supports versioned prices, effective dates and discount approvals.
Contractual constraints are already recorded in structured fields; document-only contracts require additional reviewed extraction.
Market observations are supplied through lawful research and reviewed for comparability.
Time shares retain a substantial human pricing decision despite structured inputs.
Build ranges cover one pricing unit, a limited currency set and existing approval features.
GDPR applies where customer-level pricing data identifies individuals; employee consultation depends on national rules and implementation scope.
unknowns: Pricing complexity, currencies, rebates and retrospective discounts.
Whether contractual pricing constraints are structured and complete.
The authoritative price system and permitted update interfaces.
Release authority, discount delegation and required customer notice periods.
research_questions: Can existing pricing features cover scenarios and approvals without custom code?
Which historical discount patterns explain margin leakage after accounting for product and customer mix?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings, scenario assumptions and contract exception fields.
Test effective dates, currencies and discount thresholds before release.
Resolve rejected updates and reconcile prices across systems.
Review whether approved discount changes improve realised margins.
tasks.statement: Determine price schedules and discount rates.

tasks.short: Review sales and operating records to forecast revenue and assess profitability.

steps.what: Retrieve pipeline, booked sales, costs and delivery records.
Match records and resolve inconsistent dates, account identifiers and cost allocations.
Calculate sales scenarios and margins by account, product and territory.
Write commentary explaining changes, risks and unusual results.

loop.input: Calculated scenarios, margin report and dated opportunity notes.
loop.output: Draft commentary with references for each number and stated uncertainty.
loop.check: Validate numbers against calculated tables; manager checks explanations against source notes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per report; unresolved claims become flagged blanks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover numbers but cannot reliably explain varied free-text opportunity notes.

steps.what: Choose forecast assumptions using customer context, delivery constraints and commercial judgement.
Validate profitability definitions and approve the forecast for management reporting.
Distribute approved figures and archive the reporting version.

tasks.design: Connect the {CRM}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} through configured feeds into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliation rules and scenarios shown in the {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares commentary in the {DOCS}; the sales manager selects assumptions and the finance lead approves the reporting version. The {WORKFLOW} distributes only that approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account identifiers, reporting dates and margin definitions differed across systems. Maintaining the joins and report templates cost more than periodic manual assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and faster development of small reconciliation routines reduce setup effort. Forecast arithmetic and margin calculations already have deterministic methods.
tasks.still_hard: Pipeline optimism, changing delivery dates and disputed cost allocations still need judgement. Better reporting does not establish forecast accuracy.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which customer commitments are credible and which commercial risks the figures conceal.

ambition.what: Weekly intervention on accounts with deteriorating forecast margins.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to testing assumptions and discussing margin risks. The manager can propose earlier account interventions; budget and pricing authority still follows existing delegation.

reach.task: Resolve order and delivery discrepancies affecting the sales forecast.
reach.learn: Order statuses, delivery cut-offs and the difference between bookings and recognised revenue.

evidence.claim: A CRM can provide deal probabilities and revenue forecasting assistance.
Deterministic reconciliation, scenario arithmetic and margin reporting can remove much of report preparation.
The digest provides no documented sales forecasting accuracy case supporting an accuracy improvement.

assumptions: The company sells through a maintained opportunity pipeline and records costs in the {ERP}.
An {OPS_SYSTEM} supplies delivery records where relevant; service businesses may use order records instead.
Time shares are estimates, informed by the supplied priors; judgement remains separate from report preparation.
Build ranges cover one business unit using existing infrastructure and agreed reporting definitions.
GDPR applies to customer and employee data; access is limited to necessary records.
unknowns: Available connectors, export rights and common account identifiers.
Approved margin definitions and treatment of overhead, returns and rebates.
Forecast approval authority and reporting cadence.
Whether individual employee reporting requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which existing connector and reporting features cover the required joins?
How well do current forecast assumptions perform against subsequent actuals?
new_work: Review unmatched records and disputed cost allocations.
Check draft commentary and maintain reporting definitions.
Monitor feed freshness and reconcile approved forecasts against actuals.
tasks.statement: Review operational records and reports to project sales and determine profitability.

tasks.short: Coordinate sales records, accounting, receiving and shipping, and resolve discrepancies.

steps.what: Check confirmed orders and identify incomplete sales records.
Check invoices, service charges and payment allocations against sales records.
Review receipts, dispatches and delivery holds.
Combine departmental reports and investigate mismatches.
Agree priorities, corrective actions and owners with finance and logistics.
Correct order records and record fulfilment follow-up.
Approve and post accounting corrections with supporting evidence.

tasks.design: Use native exception reports in the {CRM}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, then match their records through deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A queue in the {WORKFLOW} shows mismatches and owners; approved corrections use existing controls in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers and reporting cut-offs made reconciliation depend on departmental exports and manual investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Available APIs or scheduled exports support repeatable matching. Faster integration development makes a narrow exception queue affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Partial deliveries, service adjustments, disputed payments and accounting cut-offs need explicit treatment. Financial posting permissions must remain separated from sales decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The manager balances customer commitments, stock constraints and financial consequences across departments.

ambition.what: A daily decision on customer orders blocked by accounting or fulfilment exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The manager reviews a prioritised exception queue instead of assembling reports. They can coordinate recovery decisions earlier, while finance retains ledger approval and logistics retains dispatch authority.

reach.learn: Order identifiers, partial fulfilment and financial escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Structured order, invoice and shipment reconciliation can use deterministic rules without a model.
Native approval workflows can control order changes and ledger postings; availability depends on configuration.

assumptions: This describes a company distributing physical goods with associated services.
Step shares cover the combined process across the listed roles, rather than the manager alone.
Routine reports contain usable order or reference identifiers.
Time reductions and build ranges are estimates, not measured results.
Access and consultation ranges include GDPR controls and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether common order identifiers cross the three systems.
Which native exception reports and write interfaces are available.
The approval thresholds for order and accounting corrections.
How much service accounting follows a separate process.
research_questions: Which mismatch categories can be resolved with existing deterministic rules?
How much investigation time comes from timing differences rather than actual errors?
new_work: Maintain identifier mappings and reconciliation rules.
Investigate unmatched records and delayed feeds.
Review proposed corrections and monitor duplicate or failed writes.
Reconcile the exception queue with source-system totals.
tasks.statement: Direct, coordinate, and review sales and service accounting and record-keeping, as well as receiving and shipping.

tasks.short: Consult department heads on advertising services, equipment requirements and customer specifications.

steps.what: Gather customer requirements, product information and current service constraints.
Prepare an agenda highlighting missing specifications and conflicting requirements.

loop.input: Customer requirements, product records and service constraints from selected records.
loop.output: Consultation agenda with source references, open questions and possible conflicts.
loop.check: Every factual statement references an input; missing information stays an open question.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per agenda; unresolved conflicts return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text requirements express dependencies and contradictions that field checks alone cannot identify.

steps.what: Discuss options, resolve conflicts and agree feasible specifications and service plans.
Document agreed specifications, responsibilities and unresolved questions for confirmation.

loop.input: Written meeting notes and provisional service plan.
loop.output: Specification record and action list with owners, dates and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Each agreement traces to the notes; missing owners or dates remain blank for confirmation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguous commitments require participant confirmation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes contain varied wording and conditional agreements rather than fixed fields.

steps.what: Send confirmed actions to owners and arrange follow-up.

tasks.design: A configured view joins customer requirements in the {CRM} with approved product and service records in the {DOCS}. Bounded drafting and extraction loops prepare agendas and decision records, while the {WORKFLOW} creates tasks in the {PROJECT} after the department head confirms specifications and commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and agreements lived in free-text documents and conversations. A fixed form could organise records but could not reliably interpret conditional commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded model loops can produce source-linked drafts for review. Existing task and approval features can handle the confirmed actions.
tasks.still_hard: Negotiating competing priorities and discovering requirements that customers or departments have not stated. Preparation cannot establish technical feasibility by itself.
tasks.human_edge: Surface hidden concerns, negotiate workable compromises and recognise when apparent agreement is fragile.

ambition.what: Pre-sale specification checkpoint for bespoke orders

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling agendas and chasing actions, while consultation remains central. They can organise a specification checkpoint; technical and commercial approval rights remain with their current holders.

reach.task: Validate customer specifications before an offer is issued.
reach.learn: Requirements traceability, feasibility questions and the boundary between a proposal and a commitment.

evidence.claim: Meeting preparation and paperwork can change while negotiation and specification approval remain human.
Source-linked drafting and extraction require review for conditional or ambiguous commitments.

assumptions: The task covers cross-department planning relevant to the company's sales model.
Written notes are available; automatic recording is not required.
Step shares and build ranges are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
GDPR applies to personal data in customer requirements and notes; national rules govern any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Which department confirms equipment requirements and service feasibility.
Whether customer specifications have a consistent record location.
Who can commit delivery capacity, service scope and customer terms.
Applicable access, retention and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which missing specifications most often cause offer revisions?
Can a structured requirements form remove some agenda drafting?
Which agreements need confirmation from more than one department?
new_work: Review agenda conflicts and extracted commitments.
Resolve missing owners, dates and technical confirmations.
Maintain specification templates, source permissions and extraction checks.
tasks.statement: Confer or consult with department heads to plan advertising services and to secure information on equipment and customer specifications.

tasks.short: Advise dealers and distributors on policies and operating procedures.

steps.what: Receive a dealer's question and establish its account and topic.
Find current policies and check which provisions apply.
Prepare practical guidance for the dealer's circumstances.

loop.input: Dealer issue and manager-selected, current policy references.
loop.output: Guidance draft with references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Manager checks applicability, agreement terms and every proposed exception.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting policy returns to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but explanations must address varied free-text circumstances.

steps.what: Discuss operational changes, resolve concerns and agree actions with the dealer.
Record agreed actions, owners and follow-up dates in the account record.

tasks.design: Configure dealer case capture in the {CRM} and a policy index in the {DOCS}, filtered by agreement, territory and effective date. A bounded drafting loop prepares referenced guidance for manager approval; a structured action form creates follow-up tasks in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy versions and dealer agreements were hard to connect, while advice depended on account context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case forms and document metadata handle routing and retrieval. A small model loop can draft explanations from selected sources.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, undocumented local practice and requests for exceptions still need commercial and sometimes legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands the relationship, tests whether advice is workable and negotiates commitments.

ambition.what: A scheduled operating-policy clinic for newly appointed distributors.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time finding policies and recording actions, freeing time for dealer coaching. Existing commercial authority stays unchanged; contract exceptions still require the designated approver.

reach.learn: Policy applicability, agreement limits and when to escalate.

evidence.claim: Policy indexing, case routing and structured follow-up can use existing software configuration.
Referenced guidance drafting is plausible with bounded generation and human review; no direct case is supplied.

assumptions: The company manages a dealer or distributor channel.
Approved policies and agreements are digitally accessible.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR controls and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether dealer questions already enter the {CRM}.
Who approves policy exceptions and agreement changes.
How consistently policy versions and territory applicability are recorded.
Which national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: How often can a question be answered from current approved sources?
Does reviewed drafting save time after checking agreement-specific exceptions?
new_work: Maintain policy metadata and remove superseded guidance.
Review drafts and resolve conflicting sources.
Handle unmatched accounts and failed case capture.
tasks.statement: Advise dealers and distributors on policies and operating procedures to ensure functional effectiveness of business.

tasks.short: Prepare the sales budget and approve spending within delegated limits.

steps.what: Collect sales results, actual spending and outstanding commitments.
Calculate budget scenarios using sales targets, staffing costs and planned activities.
Agree investment priorities and trade-offs with finance and department heads.
Review and approve the budget proposal.
Enter approved allocations into the financial budget records.
Assess spending requests against priorities, available budget and delegated authority.
Record the spending decision and notify the requester.

tasks.design: Configure feeds from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} into a budget dashboard, with a deterministic scenario generator for costs and allocations. Approval flows in the {WORKFLOW} record budget and spending decisions, update the {ERP} and notify requesters; people retain investment choices and spending authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget definitions and commitments differed between systems. Spreadsheet calculations were cheap to maintain, while connecting approval records required access and agreement across teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and approval features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building missing mappings and scenario calculations; access and data definitions still need agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Investment trade-offs, uncertain sales assumptions and reliable commitment data. Financial authority and separation of duties must remain explicit.
tasks.human_edge: Choose where scarce funds have the strongest commercial value and challenge optimistic assumptions.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer reconciliations and more discussion of investment trade-offs. The manager can propose monthly reallocations; approval rights change only through explicit delegation.

reach.task: Plan territory staffing and selling activities.
reach.learn: Translate activity plans into costs, capacity assumptions and expected contribution.

evidence.claim: Budget consolidation, scenario calculations and approval routing can use deterministic rules.
Funnel provides standardised marketing data and automated reports, supporting the reporting building block.
Pipedrive offers revenue forecasting support; this does not establish forecast accuracy or budget decision quality.

assumptions: A typical process combines system records, spreadsheet scenarios and managerial approval.
Step shares and build ranges are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
The first release covers one sales budget and existing approval limits.
GDPR applies where budget inputs contain personal data; aggregated staffing costs are preferred.
unknowns: Available reporting, import and approval features in the existing systems.
Who holds budget authority and which spending thresholds apply.
Whether purchase commitments and staffing costs are complete and current.
Access requirements and whether national rules require employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing configuration replace the spreadsheet scenario calculations?
Which commitments are absent from the financial records until an invoice arrives?
Which spending decisions require commercial judgement beyond threshold checks?
new_work: Review scenario assumptions and unusual variances.
Resolve missing commitments and failed imports.
Maintain account mappings, approval limits and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Prepare budgets and approve budget expenditures.

tasks.short: Attend trade association meetings to promote products and develop industry relationships.

steps.what: Review the meeting agenda and choose relevant topics and relationship objectives.
Assemble approved product facts, examples and presentation materials.
Attend the meeting, discuss products and build relationships with participants.
Record relevant contacts, industry observations and agreed next steps.

loop.input: The manager's written meeting notes and agreed next steps.
loop.output: Draft contact updates, attributed observations and follow-up list.
loop.check: Entries trace to notes; observations retain attribution and uncertainty; contact details are verified.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per meeting; uncertain entries return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes mix observations, named contacts and conditional follow-up requests.

steps.what: Send requested product information and assign agreed follow-up.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles meeting packs from approved material in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop drafts contact updates and observations for the {CRM} and {DOCS}, while a configured flow prepares requested follow-up in the {EMAIL} for the manager's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most time was spent representing the company and building relationships. Small volumes and inconsistent notes made bespoke paperwork automation difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable templates and existing contact workflows make a small implementation practical. A bounded extraction loop can organise notes without automating live representation.
tasks.still_hard: Reputation, judgement in public discussion and the value of relationships. An attendee list does not establish permission for marketing.
tasks.human_edge: Represent the company credibly, adapt to the room and recognise useful relationships and sensitive topics.
tasks.altitude: The week changes modestly through shorter pack preparation and record entry. Representation remains human, and no new decision rights follow from the change.

reach.task: Qualify contacts after an industry meeting.
reach.learn: Distinguish a requested follow-up from general interest and record the next step accurately.

evidence.claim: Approved templates and contact workflows can support meeting preparation and follow-up.
Electronic marketing has consent and opt-out requirements; attendance alone does not establish marketing permission.
An objection to direct marketing requires that processing for that purpose stop.

assumptions: The manager attends occasional association meetings and uses approved product material.
The initial implementation uses written notes and existing presentation assets.
Step shares and build ranges are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Live representation stays within existing authority; new claims or commitments use existing approval processes.
GDPR applies to contact records; national rules determine any additional consultation requirements.
unknowns: Meeting frequency and the amount of preparation actually required.
Availability and currency of approved product materials.
Permitted uses of association contact lists.
Applicable contact retention, access and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Would existing templates and contact fields capture most of the benefit without a model loop?
Which observations are useful enough to retain and share?
How are requested follow-ups distinguished from marketing campaigns?
new_work: Review contact extraction and attributed observations.
Approve requested external follow-up.
Keep presentation templates current and maintain contact restrictions.
tasks.statement: Represent company at trade association meetings to promote products.

tasks.short: Plan sales staffing, training and performance reviews.

steps.what: Review sales demand, team capacity and vacancies.
Choose staffing needs, coverage changes and proposed recruitment.
Check staffing proposals and authorise funded recruitment or role changes.
Discuss skill gaps and choose training objectives with team supervisors.
Assign agreed courses, arrange sessions and track completion.
Assemble agreed goals, sales results and employee feedback for reviews.
Discuss performance, contextualise results and agree development actions.
Record the evaluation and agreed development actions.
Schedule development follow-ups and remind action owners.

tasks.design: Configure capacity views from the {CRM} and {HCM}, course assignments in the {LMS}, and evidence packs and review forms in the {TALENT}. The {WORKFLOW} routes staffing approvals and development reminders. People choose staffing, discuss performance and approve recorded evaluations; evidence packs contain source facts without inferred employee scores.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staffing, training and reviews used separate calendars and records. Much of the task also requires conversations and decisions that software cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing systems support forms, assignments and reminders. Small integrations can reuse approved records and reduce repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Fair evaluation requires territory context, opportunity quality and employee explanations. Employee data access and consultation may take longer than configuration.
tasks.human_edge: The manager builds trust, recognises unfair comparisons and gives feedback that an employee can act on.

ambition.what: A first-quarter development pathway for newly promoted sales supervisors.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time organising review cycles and more time coaching supervisors and planning capacity. They gain room to propose development pathways; employment and budget decision rights follow existing delegation.

reach.task: Coach representatives and follow through on development actions.
reach.learn: Observation-based feedback, fair comparison of territories and practical coaching methods.

evidence.claim: Configured learning and performance workflows can automate assignments, evidence assembly and reminders.
AI used to monitor or evaluate workers can fall within the AI Act's high-risk employment category.
Dutch works-council rules include consent rights concerning personnel monitoring arrangements; national rules vary.

assumptions: The {HCM}, {LMS} and {TALENT} hold usable records and configurable workflows.
Review forms reuse structured, human-written notes; no model rates employees.
Time shares retain the substantial conversation and coordination work indicated by the supplied priors.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine employee consultation and employment procedures.
Consent and access ranges allow consultation for a limited pilot; formal processes can take longer.

Maintain course mappings, review templates and approval routes.

tasks.statement: Plan and direct staffing, training, and performance evaluations to develop and control sales and service programs.

tasks.short: Visit franchised dealers to discuss starting or expanding leasing programmes.

steps.what: Review the dealer's sales, account history and existing leasing activity.
Prepare approved leasing terms, examples and programme requirements for the visit.
Agree a visit date and send practical arrangements.
Visit the dealer, explore concerns and discuss a feasible leasing programme.
Record dealer concerns, programme interest and agreed next steps.

loop.input: The manager's written visit notes and agreed next steps.
loop.output: Draft account update containing stated concerns, interest and actions.
loop.check: Every entry traces to a note; interest is not converted into a purchase commitment.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per visit; uncertain fields stay blank for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Visit notes vary in wording and distinguish tentative interest from agreed action.

steps.what: Send agreed information and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Configure a dealer brief in the {CRM} and generate visit packs from approved leasing records in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop drafts account updates from written visit notes, then a deterministic flow prepares agreed follow-up in the {EMAIL}; the manager approves account changes and external messages.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work depended on visits and trust, so administrative savings were modest. Dealer notes and programme materials were often maintained separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured account views and template generators can remove preparation work. Bounded extraction can reduce re-entry of notes without interpreting dealer interest as consent or commitment.
tasks.still_hard: Dealer economics, programme suitability, travel and trust. Leasing terms and commitments may require specialist review under applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the dealer's incentives, read hesitation and negotiate a programme the dealer can deliver.
tasks.altitude: Visits still dominate this work, with shorter preparation and follow-up. The manager can bring current readiness evidence to monthly discussions; contractual authority does not automatically expand.

reach.task: Follow up dealer programme interest and resolve launch prerequisites.
reach.learn: Dealer economics, leasing prerequisites and accurate recording of tentative interest.

evidence.claim: Dealer relationship work remains human while preparation, record updates and follow-up can be supported.
GDPR Article 21 requires direct marketing to stop following an objection, including related profiling.
Electronic marketing rules constrain unsolicited outreach; agreed visit follow-up needs classification by purpose.

assumptions: This task applies where franchised dealers and leasing programmes exist.
Approved leasing terms and programme requirements can populate fixed templates.
Step shares and build ranges are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Live discussion stays within existing commercial authority; binding agreements follow their separate approval process.
GDPR applies to dealer contact records; national rules determine additional leasing and consultation requirements.
unknowns: Whether this sales manager's company uses franchised dealers or leasing programmes.
Where dealer leasing activity and approved terms are recorded.
Which statements or offers require specialist approval.
Contact permissions, marketing objections and applicable national rules.
Whether travel time is included in the customer's task measurement.
research_questions: Which launch prerequisites distinguish interest from genuine dealer readiness?
Can structured visit fields replace part of the extraction loop?
Which follow-up messages are requested service information and which are direct marketing?

Resolve outdated leasing terms and missing programme prerequisites.
Maintain templates, source permissions and contact restrictions.
tasks.statement: Visit franchised dealers to stimulate interest in establishment or expansion of leasing programs.

tasks.short: Understand customer equipment needs and recommend technically suitable purchase options.

steps.what: Review the enquiry and retrieve relevant equipment specifications
Discuss intended use, site conditions, budget, and operating constraints
Record the customer's requirements and unresolved questions

loop.input: The manager's written discovery notes and a fixed equipment-requirements schema.
loop.output: Requirement fields, source references, and explicit unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate units and ranges; cite each value; never infer missing specifications; the manager approves the record.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous values remain blank for customer clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conversational notes contain requirements in varied language; a fixed form alone would require manual re-entry.

steps.what: Compare equipment options against recorded requirements
Validate technical suitability and resolve site-specific compatibility questions
Explain suitable options, trade-offs, and the recommended purchase
Prepare the written recommendation with assumptions and technical conditions
Check and send the equipment recommendation

tasks.design: Use an indexed catalogue in the {DOCS} and a requirements record in the {CRM}, with a bounded extractor to turn written discovery notes into fields for approval. A deterministic comparison app in the {WORKFLOW} filters documented specifications, exposes missing constraints, and passes the shortlist to a sales engineer. A template generator in the {DOCS} produces the recommendation from approved fields, and the manager approves sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrive conversationally, while equipment specifications use inconsistent documents and units. Expert compatibility knowledge is often undocumented.
tasks.enabler_now: A small requirements app, unit validation, constraint rules, and document templates can now be assembled with less implementation effort. Text extraction reduces re-entry but does not establish technical suitability.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions, installation interfaces, safety implications, and undocumented product limitations still require qualified judgement. Catalogue cleaning and encoding compatibility rules may dominate the cost.
tasks.human_edge: Discover the real operating need, explain trade-offs honestly, and recognise when a site assessment or specialist is necessary.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time comparing specifications and preparing documents, leaving more time for discovery and explaining trade-offs. They can offer a site-readiness brief, while technical sign-off remains with the sales engineer and commercial authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Screen basic capacity and interface requirements before detailed engineering
reach.learn: Learn specification units, operating tolerances, compatibility limits, and mandatory engineering escalation points.

evidence.claim: Known specification constraints, unit checks, and recommendation templates can be implemented deterministically.
A bounded extractor can prepare structured requirements, but technical suitability requires validated rules and qualified review.
The digest contains no documented equipment-advisory case; time savings and build ranges here are estimates.

assumptions: This task describes a business selling equipment where the sales manager handles complex enquiries with sales-engineering support.
The initial scope covers one equipment family with maintained technical specifications.
Unknown constraints block a suitability claim rather than being treated as satisfied.
The notes extractor uses written notes; call recording and transcription are outside scope.
GDPR applies where enquiries contain personal data; applicable EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules depend on the deployed use.
Build ranges are working-day effort and exclude extensive catalogue remediation or engineering-rule discovery.
unknowns: Catalogue completeness, version control, and unit consistency.
Which compatibility constraints are documented and testable.
Required engineering sign-off and site-assessment triggers.
Access rights, customer confidentiality requirements, and permitted data processing.
research_questions: Can an existing configurator cover the equipment family before building a comparison app?
Which requirements can be captured directly in a short form, reserving extraction for free-text notes?
Can historical recommendations expose missing rules without treating past decisions as technical ground truth?
new_work: Approve extracted requirements and clarify missing values.
Maintain catalogue versions, unit mappings, and compatibility rules.
Route novel configurations to sales engineering.
Check generated recommendations against technical approval before sending.
tasks.statement: Confer with potential customers regarding equipment needs, and advise customers on types of equipment to purchase.

tasks.short: Oversee regional sales managers, resolve operating problems, and agree support and staffing priorities.

steps.what: Review regional pipelines, results, and overdue customer commitments
Send staffing constraints, support requests, and unresolved team issues
Prepare the regional review agenda
Discuss performance, coach managers, and understand local constraints
Agree resource changes, escalation owners, and management actions
Record agreed actions, owners, and due dates
Check progress and chase overdue actions

tasks.design: Configure regional exception views in the {CRM} and structured manager updates in the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic generator assembles a review agenda in the {DOCS}, retaining managers' comments verbatim and linking each figure to its source. Approved actions create records in the {PROJECT}, with reminders and overdue exceptions sent through the {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational figures, local context, and action status sit in separate places. Someone must maintain shared definitions and the joins between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting, forms, and reminder features cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort needed for the remaining joins and agenda generator.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching, competing regional priorities, and sensitive staffing decisions remain human. Employee data access and consultation obligations depend on the proposed use and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what a local manager is reluctant to say, challenge explanations fairly, and negotiate support across regions.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less report preparation and more coaching and removal of cross-region obstacles. Formal staffing and budget decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan short-term coverage for customer handovers and specialist support
reach.learn: Learn workload estimation, coverage constraints, and the supervisor's escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Structured updates, template assembly, and action reminders can use deterministic technology; coaching remains human.
Pipedrive provides deal probability and next-action support, establishing available pipeline components rather than automated staff supervision.
The step shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured customer results.

assumptions: The scope is routine supervision; formal employment changes follow the existing approval process.
Action owners maintain completion status in the {PROJECT}; silence does not count as completion.
The design uses operational exceptions and does not generate employee rankings or performance scores.
GDPR applies to employee records; any later AI-based employee evaluation requires assessment under the EU AI Act and national rules.
Build ranges are working-day effort for one initial deployment; consultation and access waiting time may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Available regional reporting views and connector permissions.
Consistency of regional sales definitions and action ownership.
Delegated staffing and spending limits.
Required employee consultation, access restrictions, and retention periods.
research_questions: Can existing reporting and forms generate the agenda without custom integration?
Which operational exceptions warrant discussion rather than a routine notification?

Maintain regional definitions, exception thresholds, and access groups.
Resolve stale action records and connector failures.

tasks.short: Direct export administration, bid records, collection records and maintenance of trade requirements.

steps.what: Assign clerical priorities and review overdue administrative work.
File export correspondence and link messages to accounts and orders.
Record bid requests, deadlines and responsible sales representatives.

loop.output: Proposed bid fields with source passages and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Validate dates and account identifiers; administrator verifies scope, deadline and owner before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unreadable or conflicting requests enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Bid requests arrive in varied prose and document layouts; fixed forms handle only some requests.

steps.what: Update collection status and flag overdue or disputed balances.
Check authoritative tariff, licence and restriction sources for relevant changes.

loop.input: Changed authoritative source documents for specified classifications and destinations.
loop.output: Proposed register changes with quotations, source references and effective dates.
loop.check: Check source versions and exact values; specialist verifies applicability, classifications and legal interpretation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; missing sources, ambiguity or stale data require specialist handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Source changes can be buried in notices and annexes; structured feeds should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Resolve escalations and assign commercial or administrative follow-up.
Publish approved trade updates and assign resulting record-maintenance tasks.

tasks.design: Configure correspondence linking, bid records and collection views across the {EMAIL}, {CRM} and {ERP}, with a shared queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded extraction proposes bid fields and changes from approved {GOV_PORTAL} sources; specialist-approved updates populate the versioned register in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correspondence, bids, collections and trade notices had different formats, owners and filing routines.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record linking and workflows cover routine administration. Bounded extraction can handle document variation while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Trade classification, licensing scope and restrictions require specialist interpretation. Missing updates or incorrect effective dates can have serious consequences; automated summaries cannot authorise shipments.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sets commercial priorities and resolves disputes; the specialist determines trade-rule applicability.

ambition.what: A destination-specific bid-readiness pack reviewed by the export compliance specialist.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing records and can resolve bid or collection blockers sooner. Trade permissions, credit concessions and shipment release retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Prepare a complete export-order evidence pack.
reach.learn: Document completeness, source effective dates and when specialist approval is required.

evidence.claim: Record linking, deadlines and overdue-balance queues can mostly use deterministic workflows.
Document extraction can prepare reviewable fields, but the digest supplies no export-compliance implementation case.

assumptions: The company exports goods and has access to trade-compliance expertise.
Step shares cover the combined administrative process across the listed roles.
Correspondence with missing identifiers remains in a manual matching queue.
Collection automation updates records and queues; it does not send demands or grant concessions.
Build and remaining-time figures are estimates.
Access work covers GDPR retention and permissions, plus consultation required by national rules.

Whether structured trade-data feeds are licensed and accessible.
How many bid requests use standard forms.

Can source changes be detected completely for the relevant destinations?
Which existing controls prevent stale trade guidance from being used?

Verify trade-source changes and effective dates.
Maintain source coverage, account matching and retention rules.
Handle failed imports and monitor overdue exception queues.

tasks.short: Direct foreign sales and service outlets, set priorities, and resolve performance and delivery issues.

steps.what: Combine outlet sales, margin, backlog, and service results into a performance pack.
Read local updates and prepare the outlet review brief.

loop.input: Outlet updates, validated performance figures, and previous actions.
loop.output: A sourced review brief with discrepancies and questions.
loop.check: Validate figures against the performance pack; link qualitative claims to source passages. The sales manager reviews.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per outlet; missing or conflicting evidence becomes an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Local explanations use varied language and require summarising; calculations remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss performance, customer issues, and local constraints with the outlet manager.
Decide outlet priorities, target adjustments, and support within delegated limits.
Agree responsibilities, support, and delivery dates with the outlet manager.
Record agreed actions, owners, and deadlines in the shared action register.
Check action status and performance thresholds for emerging exceptions.
Resolve exceptions with local leaders and escalate decisions beyond delegated limits.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile outlet records from the {CRM}, {ERP}, and {OPS_SYSTEM}, then populate an outlet dashboard in {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares sourced review briefs in {DOCS}; the sales manager reviews them and personally directs outlet discussions and decisions. A structured action form in {WORKFLOW} feeds agreed commitments into {PROJECT}, where configured rules flag overdue actions and performance exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlet identifiers, currencies, reporting periods, and margin definitions differ. Management judgement and relationship work made the whole task appear unsuitable for automation, although preparation and tracking were separable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and workflow features can handle much of the support work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mappings and validation rules; bounded language models can draft briefs from varied local updates.
tasks.still_hard: Comparable margin and service measures need agreement. Local market knowledge, conflicting priorities, cross-border data access, and decisions beyond the manager's mandate still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when weak results reflect local constraints, challenge explanations without damaging trust, and negotiate credible commitments across markets.

ambition.what: Fortnightly allocation of shared sales and service support across foreign outlets.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less report assembly and status checking, leaving more time for outlet coaching and support allocation. Formal decision rights remain within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Turn outlet priorities into practical coaching and weekly team commitments.
reach.learn: Learn frontline workload constraints and how supervisors distinguish skill gaps from capacity problems.

reach.task: Assess technical causes of recurring customer and service escalations.
reach.learn: Learn product limitations and technical dependencies before promising corrective action.

Resolve stale feeds, unmatched outlet records, and inconsistent reporting definitions.

Check whether alerts identify actionable issues and adjust noisy thresholds.
Maintain brief templates and validate drafting quality when inputs change.

tasks.short: Assess sales potential and expenditure for new and existing store locations.

steps.what: Collect existing store sales, margin and operating-cost baselines.
Gather catchment, competitor and footfall evidence from geographic data services in the {OTHER}.
Calculate demand, costs, break-even and cannibalisation under alternative assumptions.
Visit the location and test assumptions about access, competition and customer behaviour.
Prepare a location recommendation with financial sensitivities and evidence gaps.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, source references and manager's site assessment.
loop.output: Draft recommendation explaining the manager's selected option and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Insert numbers directly from tables; manager verifies narrative, uncertainty and selected option.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved evidence gaps stay explicit and return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle financial tables, but interpreting varied site notes requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Challenge the recommendation and decide whether to proceed, investigate or stop.

tasks.design: Refresh store baselines in the {BI} and use deterministic imports on the {DATA_PLATFORM} for licensed geographic data from the {OTHER}. Configure a controlled scenario workbook in the {SPREADSHEET}, then generate financial tables and a reviewed narrative in the {DOCS}; investment decisions remain with the committee.
tasks.previous_blocker: External data required repeated preparation, and location models used inconsistent assumptions and source dates.
tasks.enabler_now: Repeatable imports and reusable financial models remove preparation work. Bounded drafting can turn validated results and site notes into a reviewable paper.
tasks.still_hard: Local demand, competitor reactions and cannibalisation remain uncertain. Data licences, sparse comparisons and delayed outcomes limit validation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager notices local conditions absent from datasets and judges whether the commercial concept fits the catchment.

ambition.what: A quarterly retain, refurbish or relocate review for existing stores.

tasks.altitude: The manager compares more locations and tests sensitivities with less preparation. They gain a practical role in proposing early investigations; investment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Catchment interpretation, contribution margin and structured observation.

evidence.claim: Reusable scenario models and scheduled data imports can reduce repeated location-analysis preparation.

The {BI} already exposes store sales and cost baselines.

Geographic analysis uses aggregate data, with GDPR checks for any personal data.

Review scenario assumptions and generated recommendations.
Compare realised store outcomes with approved scenarios.
Investigate missing or conflicting external evidence.
